subject: Human Evolution
title: Radiometric Dating
description: A quick win: understand Radiometric Dating.

hook.text: How do you know a bone is 2 million years old? You measure the decay of radioactive atoms trapped inside.

buildup.text: Potassium-40 decays into argon-40 at a known rate. Volcanic rock acts as a natural clock.

discovery.text: By measuring the potassium-argon ratio in layers above and below a fossil, you bracket its age.

twist.text: Carbon-14 dating only works to ~50,000 years. For older fossils, different isotopes are needed.

climax.text: Radiometric dating turned human evolution from guesswork into a precise timeline of millions of years.

punchline.text: Atoms keep time better than any clock.

quiz.question: Why can't carbon-14 date fossils older than ~50,000 years?
